title: Endpoint SLO Declaration Kit and Operational Failover Runbook for Weighted Multi-Region Fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a reusable SLO/SLI declaration kit and an operational runbook that defines how per-endpoint and per-model SLOs are declared, how error budgets are allocated and consumed across model variants and regions, and the precise policies for circuit breakers, tiered load-shedding and weighted multi-region fallback. The goal is to provide engineering and on-call teams with a single source of truth that: (1) standardizes SLI definitions for latency/availability/quality per route+model variant, (2) prescribes error budget accounting and progressive mitigation actions, and (3) documents the multi-region failover orchestration and circuit-breaker thresholds to keep service within SLO while minimizing quality regressions.
acceptance_criteria: SLO declaration template (JSON schema) committed to repo and validated against two representative endpoints (chat-streaming + embeddings).
Runbook published in Confluence with step-by-step multi-region failover play for regional outage and capacity exhaustion scenarios.
Automated error-budget dashboard (Grafana) showing burn rates per model variant and region; unit tests for SLI calculations added to monitoring repo.
Circuit breaker policy implemented in edge router config (feature-flagged) with canary rollout to a single region and documented rollback procedure.
Load-shedding policy implemented for tenant tiers (free/standard/enterprise) that enforces token quota and priority queueing; end-to-end smoke tests pass.
On-call runbook includes post-incident checklist and owner assignments; at least one simulated failover drill executed with incident playbook notes attached.
Benchmarks demonstrating <5% quality regression when failing over to lower-capacity model variants under load (measured on benchmark prompt set).
notes: We intentionally separate 'quality' SLI (model output correctness/acceptability) from latency/availability; quality SLI will be model-specific and pulled from evaluation harness outputs.
Error budgets are allocated hierarchically: route -> model-variant -> region. Policy includes borrowing rules (short-term borrow allowed up to X% of variant budget) and automated reclamation windows.
Decision: use percentile-based latency SLI (p95 for interactive routes, p99 for low-volume critical routes) and availability SLI on 5s windowed error rate for streaming routes.

Trade-offs discussed: aggressive load-shedding reduces customer-visible latency but increases request rejection rate for lower tiers. We choose a conservative safety net for enterprise tenants (degraded-model fallback before rejection).
